title: Design a Payment Gateway & Ledger (Stripe)
subtitle: Double-entry ledger, idempotency, Outbox + PSP reconciliation
functionalReqs: Process checkout payments safely with strict exactly-once financial effect despite network retries.
Maintain an immutable, auditable Double-Entry Accounting Ledger (`SUM(debits) == SUM(credits)`).
Orchestrate async external Payment Service Provider (Visa/Stripe/Bank) calls cleanly.
Run automated T+1 reconciliation against external PSP settlement files to catch silent discrepancies.

nonFunctionalReqs.rationale: Any silent divergence creates real financial & regulatory liability.
Financial auditors require tracing every cent across every timestamp.
Down checkout directly halts merchant revenue.

workedSummary.paymentWritesPerSec: 10M/day ≈ 100 QPS avg, ~400 QPS peak (2,000+ on Black Friday)
workedSummary.ledgerEntriesPerPayment: 2+ immutable rows per transfer (debit buyer / credit merchant + fee)
workedSummary.sevenYearCompliance: 10M × 3 rows × 365 × 7 × 300 B ≈ 23 TB immutable ledger history

apiContracts.purpose: Create/execute idempotent payment intent, forward to PSP, and commit double-entry journal
Verify HMAC signature and record async PSP settlement/chargeback callbacks idempotently

explorerTopology.title: Idempotent Payment Execution & Double-Entry Ledger
explorerTopology.subtitle: Idempotency lock -> External PSP call (outside SQL tx!) -> Atomic Ledger + Outbox
explorerTopology.overview: Never hold a SQL transaction open while calling an external bank/PSP over the internet (a 5-second bank stall exhausts DB connections instantly!). Instead: 1) Persist `PaymentIntent(INIT)` with `idempotency_key`, 2) Call the PSP with the SAME key, 3) Atomically commit `SUCCEEDED` + balanced Double-Entry Ledger rows + Outbox event, and reconcile async bank files nightly.
keyTakeaways: Store monetary amounts strictly as integer minor units (`amount_cents`), never floating-point `float/double`.
Never hold database row locks across slow external HTTP calls to banks/PSPs.
Every transfer writes balanced `DEBIT` + `CREDIT` immutable rows (`SUM == 0`) instead of mutating a bare `balance` integer.

nodes.label: Checkout Client
nodes.summary: Submits payment request with persistent UUID idempotency key.
failureModes: Retrying without idempotency key double-charges customers

nodes.label: Payment Executor
nodes.summary: Claims idempotency key, calls PSP outside DB lock, then commits ledger + outbox.
failureModes: Holding DB connection open during 3s PSP call drains DB pool

nodes.label: Double-Entry Ledger DB
nodes.summary: Enforces unique `idempotency_key` and balanced debit/credit entries + `outbox_events`.
failureModes: Hot single platform fee account causes row lock contention—solve by sharding fee sub-accounts!

nodes.label: External PSP / Card Network
nodes.summary: Authorizes card funds and emits async settlement files + webhooks.
failureModes: Timeout leaves payment status ambiguous—must query PSP or reconcile later

nodes.label: Outbox & T+1 Reconciler
nodes.summary: Emits receipt/webhook events via CDC and diffs internal ledger vs bank settlement files nightly.
failureModes: Unreconciled PSP timeout charges stay orphaned without automated polling

steps.info: INSERT payment_intents (idempotency_key='pay_8841', state='PENDING_PSP') -> COMMIT (release SQL conn!)
steps.payloadInspector: Unique Key Claimed -> SQL connection immediately returned to pool BEFORE calling PSP
steps.inspectorNote: Quickly committing `PENDING_PSP` prevents concurrent duplicate requests from executing while keeping DB locks open 0ms during network calls.

steps.info: Call Visa/PSP passing forward `Idempotency-Key: pay_8841` -> Authorized (180ms)
steps.inspectorNote: Passing our idempotency key upstream guarantees even if our pod crashes post-charge, retrying won't double-charge at the bank!

steps.info: Write DEBIT buyer (-$49.99), CREDIT merchant (+$48.50), CREDIT fee (+$1.49) + Outbox
steps.payloadInspector: ASSERT SUM(debits)==SUM(credits) -> State=SUCCEEDED -> Commit + CDC Outbox
steps.inspectorNote: Immutable journal entries + Outbox notify Merchant webhooks cleanly.

chaosScenarios.title: PSP Read Timeout (Ambiguous Outcome -> Async Reconciler Recovery)
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Visa/PSP network call times out at 5s after debiting the customer card, leaving PaymentIntent stuck in `PENDING_PSP`.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Payment stays `PENDING_PSP` (not naively marked FAILED!), background status-poller & T+1 Settlement Reconciler query PSP by `pay_8841`, observe `AUTHORIZED`, and complete the ledger safely.

steps.phaseTitle: 1. PSP TIMEOUT -> MARK PENDING (DO NOT FAIL)
steps.info: PSP socket timeout at 5,000ms -> Payment remains PENDING_PSP; polling job scheduled
steps.payloadInspector: CRITICAL: Do NOT tell user 'Failed' without confirming PSP status—bank might have succeeded!
steps.inspectorNote: Treating ambiguous timeouts as `PENDING` prevents double-charges when users try another card.

steps.info: Poller queries PSP(`pay_8841`) -> finds `ch_9912 AUTHORIZED` -> commits ledger cleanly!
steps.payloadInspector: Reconciled: PENDING_PSP -> SUCCEEDED + Double-Entry Ledger balanced
steps.inspectorNote: Automated reconciliation + T+1 settlement file diffs close every distributed consistency gap.

tradeoffs.option: Double-Entry Immutable Ledger + Out-of-Tx PSP Call
pros: Zero held DB locks during slow bank RPCs
cons: Higher row write volume (2–3 rows per tx)
Needs async poller/reconciler for ambiguous timeouts
tradeoffs.bestFor: Payment gateways, digital wallets, marketplace payouts, billing systems

cons: No audit history, prone to silent race conditions, impossible to verify historical balances

deepDives.title: Eliminating Hot Row Contention on Platform Fee Accounts
deepDives.bottleneck: Every payment credits the single `platform_revenue` account row—creating severe row lock contention at 2,000 QPS.
deepDives.solution: Shard hot system accounts into `platform_revenue#0..31` (pick random bucket per transaction) and sum all 32 buckets when reporting total platform revenue.
deepDives.tradeoff: Reads aggregate 32 sub-accounts in exchange for 32x higher concurrent write throughput.

deepDives.title: Integer Minor Units vs Floating Point
deepDives.bottleneck: `0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004` in IEEE-754 floats causes penny drift during millions of ledger sums.
deepDives.solution: Store every amount as `BIGINT amount_minor_units` alongside ISO-4217 currency scale (e.g. USD cents, JPY yen).
deepDives.tradeoff: Display layer formats decimals explicitly per currency precision.

criteria: Persists client idempotency key & forwards to PSP
Releases SQL lock BEFORE calling external PSP
Handles PSP timeouts as PENDING, not failed
Adds async poller + T+1 settlement reconciliation
